Hysteresis losses: When a ferromagnetic material is subjected to a cyclically varying magnetic field (like in a transformer core), the B-H curve traces out a loop rather than a single curve. The area enclosed by this loop represents the energy dissipated per unit volume per cycle. This energy is lost as heat. The loss occurs because the magnetization process is not perfectly reversible—there's an energy barrier that must be overcome as the material is driven from one magnetization state to another.
